note: Seeded 5 Sep 2026, WP-11.3 Tranche 2, the mid-nineteenth-century city house cluster. No HABS survey with written historical and descriptive data was resolved for this building from here; the searches that failed are listed in the cluster's report. A record with references and no survey block is complete, and inventing one would be worse than the gap. The one intact interior in the cluster, and the reason it earns a place: the National Historic Landmark case, as Wikipedia summarises it, is that this is 'the only Victorian era row house in Boston's Back Bay to maintain the integral relationship between the exterior architectural shell and the original interior plan'. The italianate-townhouse node asserts a section -- basement kitchen, raised parlour floor, bedrooms above -- and this is the surviving building against which that section could be checked, including the service rooms that every other precedent has lost.
